mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which causes negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is already above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of at least 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising energy prices.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the effective federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in real savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average signals a liquidity trap environment, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) alongside stable consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% month-over-month) indicates rising real household purchasing power, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when credit spreads widen by more than 100 bps.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 6-month averages signals broad-based supply contraction, which elevates input costs and reduces earnings visibility, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of falling energy prices.
